note: THE ELM LEAF'S SURFACE (T-3247). The owner asked on 2026-10-29 for the elms to be improved from freely licensed elm photographs. The grown trees' leaf blades are painted outlines; this photograph supplies the surface laid inside the elm's: its pinnate veins, its mottle and the light across its fold, as lightness only. The painted outline, twig and placement, and the July colour the zone records give the crown, are unchanged.
what_it_supplies: the upper-surface texture of an American elm leaf (Ulmus americana): its straight, close lateral veins and mottle, sampled as lightness into the elm tiles of assets/textures/trees/leaf_atlas.*
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about a tree that stood in Chicago in 1812, 1835 or 1904; it is a modern leaf from the Great Smoky Mountains, a botanical analogue for the species' habit (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-tree-architecture-2743)
the leaf's colour in the scene: the atlas keeps its near-neutral green and the zone records' July colour stays in charge of the hue
the leaf's outline: the elm blade's shape is still drawn by tools/generate_tree_atlas.py
